notes: Country-level VIZA RAG seed for philippines. This file is the source of truth for this country's visitor/tourism visa knowledge and is designed to evolve alongside the country-specific form-filling workflow.

documents.title: Philippines Visitor Visa Eligibility and Chinese Tourist Exemption

chunks.title: Chinese passport tourism route for Philippines
chunks.content: For Chinese ordinary passport holders planning short tourism travel to the Philippines, VIZA AI must first determine whether the current Chinese-national short-visitor exemption applies. If it does not apply, route the traveller to the separate PH_TEMPORARY_VISITOR_VISA process. Confirm nationality, stay length, purpose, accommodation, return or onward ticket, passport validity and the separate eTravel declaration before presenting an application route.

chunks.title: Philippines 14-day visa-free entry for Chinese tourists
chunks.content: The Philippine Embassy/Department of Foreign Affairs notice at the official source URL states that, effective 16 January 2026, Chinese nationals may enter the Philippines without obtaining a visa for stays up to 14 days for tourism or business visitor purposes, subject to the stated conditions. The notice lists a passport valid at least six months beyond the contemplated stay, confirmed hotel accommodation/booking, and return or onward ticket. Treat this as a time-bounded policy and re-check the official DFA/Bureau of Immigration instructions before departure.

chunks.title: Philippines longer or non-tourist stay route
chunks.content: If the user plans to stay more than 14 days, work, study, reside, or conduct activities outside tourism/business visitor scope, do not present the exemption as sufficient. Route them to PH_TEMPORARY_VISITOR_VISA or the appropriate consular route and ask for the exact stay length and purpose.

documents.title: Philippines eTravel Arrival and Departure Declaration

chunks.title: Philippines eTravel is an independent declaration
chunks.content: The official eTravel portal at https://etravel.gov.ph/ is a standalone arrival/departure declaration. It is not a Temporary Visitor Visa and does not decide whether a traveller is visa-exempt. Travellers must follow the portal's current registration window and preserve the official QR code/reference returned after successful submission.

chunks.title: Philippines eTravel scope and confirmation
chunks.content: Use the current official portal and customs/health instructions to determine the declaration's applicable sections. Check passport, transport, Philippines address, health and customs answers before final submission. A declaration confirmation is not an entry guarantee; immigration, health and customs authorities make the final decision.

documents.title: Philippines eTravel Arrival Card Intake Requirements

chunks.title: Philippines eTravel channel and form scope
chunks.content: Philippines eTravel is a standalone arrival/departure declaration package, not a 9(a) Temporary Visitor Visa field group. Official source URLs reviewed for this seed: https://etravel.gov.ph/ ; https://customs.etravel.gov.ph/frequently-asked-questions ; https://chongqingpcg.dfa.gov.ph/example-pages/news-press-releases/1167-philippines-to-allow-visa-free-entry-for-14-days-for-chinese-nationals. eTravel registration is free and its timing and QR/reference requirements must be confirmed on the official portal before travel. Keep visa/eVisa eligibility and 9(a) consular visa advice in separate Philippines visa packages.

chunks.title: Philippines eTravel fields to collect before filling the form
chunks.content: Collect only the official eTravel declaration data needed for the standalone arrival-card package: personal identity, passport, nationality, country of birth/residence, occupation, contact details, arrival/departure dates, travel type, transport type, flight or vessel details, origin country, port of entry, Philippines address, purpose of travel, health symptoms declaration, baggage/customs declarations, currency declaration, and final traveller declaration.

chunks.title: Philippines eTravel evidence and review checklist
chunks.content: Before submission, review passport data, flight or vessel details, Philippines address, health answers, customs/baggage answers, currency declaration, and final declaration. After successful official submission, preserve the eTravel QR code, reference number, official confirmation page screenshot/download, and portal response summary. Do not treat a normal portal screenshot as success. Do not guarantee entry; Philippine border, health, customs, and immigration authorities make the final decision.

chunks.title: Standard passport identity-field answer rules
chunks.content: Standard-answer identity fields must be answered from the applicant's passport biodata page, MRZ, official identity document, or the official dropdown options. This applies to passport number, name, date of birth, sex, nationality, issuing country, issue date, expiry date, issuing authority, place of issue, and passport/document type. For issuing authority or place-of-issue questions, do not infer the answer from the pickup city, residence city, application country, or travel destination; copy the exact Authority / Issuing authority / Place of issue wording printed on the passport if present. For Chinese ordinary passports, newer valid passports may show National Immigration Administration, PRC / 中华人民共和国国家移民管理局; older valid passports may show MPS Exit & Entry Administration / 公安部出入境管理局. If the passport prints a different authority, use the passport text. For passport type, select Ordinary / Regular / Normal only for ordinary personal passports; select Diplomatic, Official, Service, Special, Travel document, Refugee, or Other only when the document explicitly indicates that type. Official sources reviewed for this standard field rule include China National Immigration Administration certificate-issuing-authority notices and the Passport Law of the People's Republic of China; the passport biodata page remains the final source for the applicant's individual answer.

chunks.content:
Official-source field answer norms for philippines.
Use these norms only as filling guidance; if a live official form, passport, or uploaded document shows a more specific value, that document controls the answer.

Crawled source URLs: https://chongqingpcg.dfa.gov.ph/example-pages/news-press-releases/1167-philippines-to-allow-visa-free-entry-for-14-days-for-chinese-nationals ; https://etravel.gov.ph/ ; https://customs.etravel.gov.ph/frequently-asked-questions

Issue, expiry, and validity fields:
- Only the verified QR Code by BOQ upon your arrival at the airport/seaport is valid for your travel.

Travel plan and port fields:
- You may only register within 72 hours prior to your arrival or departure in the Philippines.
- Travelers are enjoined to present their eTravel QR code to flight boarding.
- You may only register within 3 days (or 72 hours) prior to your arrival in the Philippines.

Answering rule: for closed-list fields, prefer the exact official option label/value. For document-backed fields, copy the passport, official identity document, application account, itinerary, invitation, accommodation, insurance, funds, or uploaded support document rather than guessing from a city, country, or prior answer.

chunks.title: Philippines visitor visa is separate from eTravel
chunks.content: Use PH_TEMPORARY_VISITOR_VISA only when a deterministic passport, purpose and stay rule confirms a visa-required route. The Philippines eTravel declaration is separate and must not be treated as a visa or as proof of visa eligibility.

documents.title: Philippines Temporary Visitor Visa Form Requirements

chunks.title: Philippines visitor visa application preparation
chunks.content: For travellers deterministically routed to a Philippines temporary visitor visa, prepare the official channel's identity, passport, residence, contact, travel, accommodation, finance, photograph and supporting-document fields. Keep eTravel traveller declaration fields in the separate PH_ETRAVEL_ARRIVAL_CARD workflow.
